headline: Approved a winter lighting contract with SavATree, a one-year snow plow contract extension, and revoked Jacob Perdue's street entertainer permit.
summary: Lt. Governor John Rodgers spoke with commissioners about ways to engage the state on Marketplace challenges, including mental health, addiction, and crime. Staff reported that the budget is on track and about half of fundraising is complete.
decisions: Approved the winter lighting contract with SavATree, LLC, unanimously.
Approved a one-year extension of the snow plow contract, unanimously.
Revoked Jacob Perdue's street entertainer permit, unanimously.

6. Discussion with Lieutenant Governor John Rodgers on Ways to Engage with the 
State Regarding the Challenges of the Marketplace 
 
Lt. Gov Rodgers Introduced himself and spoke to his background and office. 
 M. Bouchett asked about current affairs in the Capitol. 
o J. Rogers responded. Spoke in depth on issues of Cost of Living, Property Taxes, Electric 
Rates, Economy, Unhoused and Crime.  
 M. Bouchett asked, “What are the best ways for us to engage the state.”  
o J. Rogers responded, starts at ground level. Spoke to his experience working with those in 
recovery. 
 L. Magoon asked about the Center in Waterbury, been closed for 15 years. Asked about plans to bring 
more mental health services back to the state. 
o J. Rogers responded, spoke to lots of talk about this issue, not much plan from Administration 
+ Legislature. Doesn’t believe a centralized large facility is the right choice. Bottom-up 
support from community is needed to enact change.  
 L. Magoon continued to ask what will it take to get the Governor on board to take action.
Burlington Planning Commission Minutes  
 
 
o J. Rogers responded, many communities dealing with the same issue on different levels. 
Community legislators need to get on board first.  
 M. Bouchett asks if the legislature believes unhoused in a serious problem. 
o J. Rogers responded; it will take leadership and courage on both local and state levels to find 
solutions.  
 E. Monsen added law enforcement and legal system needs support to tackle ground level issues. 
o J. Rogers responded; accountability is what is missing in addition to healthcare services. Law 
enforcement needs to have the tools and ability to tackle these issues.  
 K. Alnasrawi; referenced a recent drug sting operation in City Hall Park in which almost all arrested 
were not charged and released. What is it about our justice system or criminal code that is allowing this 
to happen? 
o J. Rogers responded that incarceration is expensive and enforcement is up to local law 
enforcement. Spoke to need for treatment and accountability.  
 K. Alnasrawi responded by asking about recovery beds, how opioid settlement funds 
are being distributed, where are the beds?  
 J. Rogers responded, spoke to the treatment that has been created, 
acknowledged that there is a long way to go. 
 M. Moore asked about bed capacity. What plan exist to address comorbid mental health and addiction 
issues. No facility of this type exists in VT. 
o J. Rogers responded; there is no current plan to address this gap in care.  
 M. Moore asked about two-week program. Given that rehab is rarely linear, are there plans for longer 
inpatient treatment or greater increase in step-down programs?  
o J. Rogers, supports additional step-down programs in which the capacity has grown.   
 B. Holt spoke to issues of division and the narrative of Burlington “Not being a part of VT”, “Not 
wanting solutions” “We get the issues but not the funding and the blame without the support”  
o J. Rogers responded; “Burlington is Vermont’s City” Supported her comments. 
 E. Monsen stated he believes we need more regional collaboration. Also stated Low Barrier Shelters 
need Low Barrier Jobs.  
o J. Rogers responded; trades are an excellent path to workforce reentry.  
 L. Magoon wants to see VT learn from other states. Central focus on looking at what other states are 
doing.  
 C. Haessly talked about bail and without it you get a revolving door. Job training is critical for 
rehabilitation. States having a third option to rehab or jail is needed.  
 L. Magoon spoke about Lund and Mercy Connections.  
 M. Bouchett wrapped up; requested that the state invest in Burlington to develop a model to implement 
else ware in the state.  
 
C. Haessly made an announcement.

1. S. McGinnis; CSM is looking for a 1-year extension.

8. Revoking Jacob Perdue’s Street Entertainer Permit 
 
1. S. McGinnis; Numerous issues with this individual and with Police.  
J. Perdue has been made aware of all infractions and was not present at this meeting. He has not yet 
been trespassed; permit revoked instead.  
 
Action: Motion to Revoke Jacob Perdue’s Street Entertainer Permit  
Motion by: C. Haessly  
Seconded by: E. Monsen  
Vote: Unanimous  
 
  
9. Reports  
S. McGinnis reported budget is on track. Just about half of fundraising complete. Spending is on track and 
budgeted for.  
Director’s report 
S. McGinnis: 
 The Marketing Manager position currently held by Jessica Dudley has been posted. 
 Chief Burke has already posted overtime patrol shifts for the holiday season, they will be paying 
for these shifts out of their budget. 
 Hot Spots meetings continuers, camera trailer remains on City Hall Park. Two weeks ago, 
Downtown meeting. 
 Fall programming, huge September and October, Cheese the Day was a massive success. Party on 
the Bricks, turnout numbers continue to go up. Construction Fest, 2,000 attendees, City Hall Park 
packed. Coming up, Howl’ween costume contest, Whizbang’s Trick or Treat event. 
 Bulk of attention now turning to holiday season, website go live 11/9. Two trees being considered 
for CSM. 
 S. McGinnis gave a full report to City Council at the start of the month. 
 No change in storefront vacancy.  
K. Alnasrawi; An offer has been made to a new Police Chief. This should be brought before City Council 
very soon.  
Chair’s Report 
M. Bouchett: 
 UVM Parents Weekend, was great downtown. 
 Hundred-Bed Shelter, toured old Gardener’s Supply location. Could be a very viable spot.
